canonical_semi_arid_wheat.query: SOC 0.3%, low rainfall (320mm), monoculture wheat, semi-arid region. What interventions do you recommend?
canonical_semi_arid_wheat.scientific_summary: Diagnostic evaluation of the submitted environmental profile reveals an agroecosystem under acute compound stress. Soil Organic Carbon (SOC) at 0.30% is critically depleted relative to the regional semi-arid target of 1.50% (-80.0% deficit), dropping well beneath the biophysical threshold of 0.50% where soil microbial resilience and structural macroaggregation collapse. With mean annual precipitation of 320 mm against a potential evapotranspiration demand of ~1200 mm (Aridity Index AI = 0.267, high moisture stress), uninterrupted wheat monoculture exacerbates fine capillary moisture losses and accelerates wind erosion. Under these biophysical constraints, high-transpiration cover crops or deep plowing are prohibited due to acute risk of cash-crop water theft. We recommend a phased dual-tier strategy: (1) Dryland perimeter and parkland agroforestry featuring Faidherbia albida / Acacia shelterbelts to buffer wind shear and restore leaf litter carbon; coupled with (2) Strip intercropping with drought-tolerant legumes (Chickpea / Pigeonpea) with stubble mulch retention to fix biological nitrogen, stimulate arbuscular mycorrhizal networks, and arrest erosive topsoil loss.
